decision_reason: SET is a distinct NASA-DEVELOP software product for modeling landscape skyglow from remote-sensing data. NASA's current Technology Transfer Catalog page identifies the exact product and its Download Now link resolves to this repository; the NASA DEVELOP documentation identifies version 0.0.1, the Wyoming Cross-Cutting team/NPS partnership, and installation, run, and map-generation guidance. The project-specific NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 is OSI-approved. Although the repository is quiet, NASA's current exact-product distribution page still links this source, so it is Maintained rather than Active.

government_provenance.note: NASA DEVELOP's official documentation says the Wyoming Cross-Cutting team created SET in partnership with the National Park Service and Wyoming Stargazing. NASA's LAR-19184-1 catalog entry names SET and its Download Now link resolves to this exact NASA-DEVELOP repository.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Python skyglow application/source and documentation without credentials; NASA's current Software Catalog links directly to it.

eligible_license.note: The live LICENSE.md is NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3, names NASA and the exact LAR-19184-1 Skyglow Estimation Toolbox, and grants worldwide use, reproduction, distribution, modification, and redistribution. OSI approves this exact version: https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3.

primary_evidence.note: The exact-product documentation says Current Version v0.0.1 and explains installation, required packages, input data, and generating skyglow maps. NASA's current LAR-19184-1 catalog page describes the reusable light-pollution model for park/resource decision makers and its Download Now link points to the reviewed repo; this satisfies the agency-published versioned-product plus user-guidance path. The page and linked docs are product-specific, not an inventory label.

decision_reason: SWIM is an identifiable NASA Langley surface-water index and monitoring tool with publicly available JavaScript sources and a project-specific NASA-1.3 grant. Hold because the repository contains only two Earth Engine scripts and the license: it has no user/install instructions, README, or versioned software release, and no independent/current operational use was verified. The current NASA Software Catalog describes the exact tool and links this source, but that listing alone does not fill the notability/maturity gap.

decision_reason: VOCAL is a distinct NASA-supported application for visualizing CALIPSO satellite data, annotating regions, and sharing findings through a database. The NASA Software Catalog identifies and currently distributes this exact source; the NASA DEVELOP/CALIPSO project site explains the funded purpose, and the project has versioned release 1.15.2b plus installation instructions and a user tutorial. Its exact NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 is OSI-approved. The code is quiet since 2017, but the current NASA product page still links the same code and its guidance, so the appropriate status is Maintained, not Active.

government_provenance.note: The official NASA-DEVELOP project site identifies VOCAL as a community project funded under NASA DEVELOP and the CALIPSO science team and explains the exact CALIPSO visualization/sharing product. NASA's LAR-18710-1 Software Catalog record names VOCAL and links this repo.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Python application, documentation source, and project-specific LICENSE.md without credentials; NASA's current catalog download route resolves to the exact repository.

eligible_license.note: The repository's actual NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 names NASA and the exact LAR-18710 / VOCAL software and grants worldwide use, reproduction, modification, distribution, and redistribution rights. OSI approves exact NASA-1.3: https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact-product page describes researchers loading CALIPSO data, annotating regions, and exporting them to a shared research database; its Download Now link points to this repo. The official project site identifies NASA funding, while the repo contains versioned release 1.15.2b (2017-05-15) and installation/user tutorials (including setup steps and CALIPSO HDF visualization workflow). The current NASA catalog route maintains exact product/source parity despite old source activity.

decision_reason: Data Curtains is publicly available NASA GIBS-associated Cesium demo code, but the exact scope of its license and whether it is a stand-alone reusable NASA software product are unresolved. The repository's LICENSE.md says the code was developed at NASA/GSFC for ESDIS, but its attached NOSA 1.3 agreement formally designates GSC-17111-1, version 0.6.2, Worldview Satellite Imagery and Downloading Tool—not Data Curtains. The README describes an exploration/demo with quick-start commands, and the latest source activity is 2021; no current exact-product support/use or release/version evidence was found.

government_provenance.note: The repo's own license header says this code was originally developed at NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center for the Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS) project, and its public NASA GIBS organization/repository and support@earthdata.nasa.gov contact provide first-party context. This establishes NASA origin but not that the Worldview grant below covers all Data Curtains code.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Cesium web application source, demo, and LICENSE.md without credentials; README provides npm install/npm start steps.

eligible_license.note: Although the document contains NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 language and NASA/GSFC copyright text, the formal agreement identifies Government Agency Original Software Designation GSC-17111-1, version 0.6.2 and Original Software Title Worldview Satellite Imagery and Downloading Tool. No primary evidence establishes Data Curtains as a modification/part of that designated Worldview software or a separate Data Curtains NOSA grant; do not assume this grant covers the assigned project.

primary_evidence.note: The README calls the code 'Exploring data curtains using Cesium' and links a live demo with npm run instructions, but provides no versioned product release or evidence of use/support as a distinct NASA product. Repository activity ends 2021-04-07; current NASA GIBS materials do not establish this exact demo's present operational role. User guidance alone does not satisfy the baseline's maturity/notability pathway.
